about.purpose: Curated catalogue of lab analytes with first-class support: identity (LOINC), unit conversion, reference context, biological variation, artifact rules, and goal relevance. Data only — all logic lives in algorithms/labs.ts.
about.keying: Every analyte is keyed by LOINC. Matching is on code, NEVER on display text: 'Vitamin D' could be 25-OH total, D3 only, 1,25-dihydroxy or a urine result, and a text match silently mismaps the result to the wrong analyte. Aliases exist for MANUAL ENTRY SEARCH ONLY and are never used to match an imported Observation.
about.unitsPolicy: canonicalUnit is what US ambulatory labs report, because that is what a user's results arrive in. `units` maps every recognised source unit to a conversion into the canonical unit. A unit not present in `units` is NOT converted — the value is stored and displayed verbatim. See integration-health-records.md §5.6: a wrong conversion on a lab value is worse than no conversion.

conversionKinds.identity: Same physical quantity, different label. ng/mL and ug/L are exactly equal.
conversionKinds.linear: canonical = raw * factor + (offset ?? 0). offset exists for HbA1c, which is affine, not proportional.
conversionKinds.refuse: Deliberate refusal. Store verbatim, display un-normalized, show `reason`.

about.rangePolicy: The lab's own referenceRange on the Observation ALWAYS wins — reference intervals are assay- and laboratory-specific. `generalRange` here is used ONLY when the lab supplied none, and must be visibly labelled as a general adult range, not the user's. It is deliberately null for every analyte too age-, sex- or assay-dependent to state responsibly.
about.goalContextPolicy: An optional range that is not the lab's, justified by `rationale`, `source` and `confidence`, tied to specific goals. Per integration-health-records.md §9.4 it never displaces the lab's range, never fires an alert on its own, and is omitted wherever it cannot be defended. Validation: goalContext without rationale AND source is a hard error.

biologicalVariationSnapshot.source: EFLM Biological Variation Database official API
biologicalVariationSnapshot.policy: CVi is the EFLM serum/plasma or whole-blood meta-estimate. CVa remains an assay-imprecision assumption unless separately cited; source verification of CVi does not turn CVa into a measured fact.

biologicalVariationProvenance.verified: Confirmed against a cited source during research.
biologicalVariationProvenance.unverified: Widely reproduced Ricos/EFLM figure, recalled but NOT re-checked against source. MUST be re-verified against biologicalvariation.eu before ship. See integration-health-records.md §12.7.
biologicalVariationProvenance.derived: Not published for this analyte; propagated from a related one. Reasoning stated.

about.clinicalFloorRationale: An absolute delta below which no change is reported however statistically significant. Exists because for tightly-controlled analytes (sodium, calcium, albumin, MCV, HbA1c) the reference change value is smaller than physiologically trivial day-to-day movement. A statistically significant change is not a clinically important one.
about.criticalPolicy: criticalLow/criticalHigh are set OUTSIDE the envelope of published hospital critical-value lists, not at them. Hospital lists assume an acutely ill inpatient and a clinician standing by; a consumer app has neither, and no repeat-and-verify step. null means this analyte can never fire a critical prompt. Anchored on CAP Q-Probes (Arch Pathol Lab Med 2007;131(12):1769). NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW BEFORE SHIP.

goals.strength: Strength and hypertrophy, 3x/week with a trainer.
goals.restricted_diet: A user-reported restricted diet or food allergy.

about.goalRangeCaution: No goalContext exists for testosterone, free testosterone, SHBG, estradiol, DHEA-S, TSH, free T4, eGFR, ALP or any CBC index. These are strongly age-, sex-, assay- and time-of-day-dependent, and an 'optimal' number for them is the most common piece of nonsense in this product category.

cbc.loincNote: 57021-8 = CBC W Auto Differential panel. 58410-2 = CBC panel, no differential. 57782-5 = manual differential.

cmp.loincNote: 24323-8 = Comprehensive metabolic 2000 panel. 24322-0 is the legacy 1998 panel.

bmp.loincNote: 51990-0 = Basic metabolic panel - Blood; 24321-2 = Basic metabolic 2000 panel, also very common.

lipid.loincNote: 24331-1 = Lipid 1996 panel (calculated LDL) — the most common Quest/LabCorp report code. 57698-3 = lipid panel with direct LDL.

iron.loincNote: 50190-8 = Iron and Iron binding capacity panel. WARNING: 24361-8 is a DEPRECATED hemogram/platelet/differential panel and is frequently miscited as the iron panel. Do not use it.

thyroid.loincNote: There is no single canonical thyroid panel LOINC. 24348-5 = Free T4 and TSH panel is the closest common one.

vitamins.loincNote: No standard panel code; vitamins are usually ordered individually.

externalIdAliases.$comment: medication-effects.json (owner: medication-effects) references analytes by a hyphenated id vocabulary that differs from ours. That file is not ours to edit, so the crosswalk lives here. Consumers resolving a medication labEffect MUST map through this table before looking up an analyte. An id mapping to null has no counterpart in this catalogue and the effect cannot be attached to a result.

loincTraps: 2286-3 is Follitropin (FSH), NOT RBC folate. RBC folate is 2283-0. This is exactly the silent-mismap failure the LOINC keying exists to prevent.
24361-8 is a deprecated hemogram panel, frequently miscited as the iron/TIBC panel. Use 50190-8.
13521-0 is NOT SHBG. Use 13967-5 (Moles/volume, nmol/L) or 2942-1 (Mass/volume).
1989-3 is 25-OH vitamin D3 ONLY, not D2+D3 total. Total is 62292-8.
Lp(a) mass (10835-7, mg/dL) and molar (43583-4, nmol/L) are separate analytes and are NOT interconvertible. Route on the reported unit, never merge the series.
hs-CRP (30522-7) and standard CRP (1988-5) must stay distinct. Merging them corrupts the cardiovascular strata.
Fasting glucose (1558-6) and random glucose (2345-7) are separate codes. Do not merge — fasting state is the whole point.
HbA1c as % is 4548-4; as IFCC mmol/mol it is 59261-8. Never apply the affine conversion to a value carrying the wrong code.

cholesterol_total.whatItMeasures: All the cholesterol carried in your blood, across every lipoprotein. On its own it is the least informative number on a lipid panel — it says nothing about how the cholesterol is distributed, and ApoB or LDL-C tell you far more.

ldl_calculated.loincDisplay: Cholesterol in LDL [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by calculation
ldl_calculated.whatItMeasures: Cholesterol carried in low-density lipoprotein particles, calculated rather than measured — usually by the Friedewald or Martin-Hopkins equation, both of which derive it from total cholesterol, HDL and triglycerides. Because triglycerides are one of the inputs, a non-fasting or high-triglyceride sample makes calculated LDL less reliable.

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult optimal ceiling for primary prevention.

biologicalVariation.note: Calculated LDL inherits the triglyceride assay's error on top of its own.

artifactRules.mechanism: Calculated LDL uses triglycerides as an input, and triglycerides rise substantially after a meal — so a non-fasting sample degrades this number specifically.
artifactRules.discriminator: A direct LDL assay, or a fasting redraw.

ldl_direct.loincDisplay: Cholesterol in LDL [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by Direct assay
ldl_direct.whatItMeasures: LDL cholesterol measured directly rather than calculated. Unaffected by fasting state, which is why labs use it when triglycerides are high.
ldl_direct.doNotMergeReason: Direct and calculated LDL are different measurements and disagree systematically, particularly at high triglycerides. Plotting them as one series manufactures trends.

hdl.loincDisplay: Cholesterol in HDL [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
hdl.whatItMeasures: Cholesterol carried in high-density lipoprotein. Higher is generally associated with lower cardiovascular risk, though trials raising HDL pharmacologically have not reduced events — so it is better read as a marker than a target.

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult floor for men; the equivalent figure for women is higher (~50).

triglycerides.whatItMeasures: Circulating fat. More than any other lipid number this one reflects what you did in the last day — recent carbohydrate and alcohol intake, and whether you ate before the draw.
movedUpBy: Eating in the hours before the draw

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult ceiling; <100 is often described as optimal.

goalContext.rationale: Guideline documents describe <100 mg/dL as optimal rather than merely acceptable, and triglycerides are one of the lipid measures most responsive to the weight loss and training already in this plan — so it is a number the user can actually move.
goalContext.source: NCEP ATP III optimal category; widely restated in subsequent guidance.

biologicalVariation.source: EuBIVAS / Aarsand; desirable APS 9.90%

artifactRules.mechanism: Triglycerides rise substantially after a meal and peak 3-5 hours later. A non-fasting result is not comparable with a fasting one.
artifactRules.discriminator: Fasting redraw, or compare only against other non-fasting results.

artifactRules.mechanism: Alcohol raises triglycerides acutely.

apob.loincDisplay: Apolipoprotein B [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
apob.whatItMeasures: A count of the atherogenic particles in your blood — every LDL, VLDL and Lp(a) particle carries exactly one ApoB. Because it counts particles rather than the cholesterol inside them, it does not get fooled when particles are cholesterol-poor, which is why it tracks risk better than LDL-C.

generalRange.note: Approximate adult population reference ceiling; labs vary.

goalContext.rationale: ApoB is the better discriminator of cardiovascular risk where it disagrees with LDL-C, and guideline bodies increasingly express primary-prevention targets around 80 mg/dL, with lower figures in high-risk groups.
goalContext.source: European Atherosclerosis Society consensus on ApoB; restated in several national lipid guidelines.
goalContext.caveat: Targets differ substantially by baseline risk, and this is an area of active guideline change. Contested enough to state as such.

biologicalVariation.note: More stable than LDL-C, which is part of why it is a better serial marker.

lipoprotein_a_mass.loincDisplay: Lipoprotein a [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

nmol/L.reason: There is no universal mg/dL to nmol/L conversion for Lp(a). Apolipoprotein(a) has a size-polymorphic KIV-2 repeat, so mass per particle varies between people; published factors around 2.0-2.5 are population averages that are wrong for any given individual. Molar results are tracked as a separate analyte.

lipoprotein_a_mass.whatItMeasures: A genetically determined lipoprotein particle that carries independent cardiovascular risk. Essentially fixed for life and barely responsive to diet or training — which makes it a one-time test rather than something to trend.
movedDownBy: Very little — it is largely not modifiable by lifestyle

biologicalVariation.note: Not a trending analyte. One measurement in a lifetime is the usual advice.

lipoprotein_a_molar.loincDisplay: Lipoprotein a [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma
lipoprotein_a_molar.whatItMeasures: Lp(a) reported as particle concentration rather than mass. Increasingly the preferred form, because it is not distorted by isoform size the way the mass assay is.

non_hdl_cholesterol.loincDisplay: Cholesterol non HDL [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
non_hdl_cholesterol.whatItMeasures: Total cholesterol minus HDL — a stand-in for all the atherogenic particles. Close in spirit to ApoB, and unaffected by fasting.
non_hdl_cholesterol.neverComputeReason: Display only when the lab reported it. We do not derive it from total cholesterol and HDL, because a computed number sitting in a results table is indistinguishable from a measured one.

glucose_fasting.loincDisplay: Fasting glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
glucose_fasting.whatItMeasures: Blood sugar after an overnight fast — the simplest read on how well your body is holding glucose steady when nothing is coming in.

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult normal fasting range; 100-125 is the prediabetes band.

critical.note: Set outside the CAP envelope (typical hospital limits ~50 and ~540 mg/dL, with institutional lows spanning 27-60 and highs 270-720). Deliberately conservative for a consumer app.

artifactRules.mechanism: This code specifically means a fasting draw. If fasting was not actually observed, the value is not a fasting glucose regardless of what the code says.
artifactRules.discriminator: Confirm fasting; HbA1c is unaffected by the last meal.

glucose_random.whatItMeasures: Blood sugar without a stated fasting state — which limits what can be read from it, because a value after a meal and a value after twelve hours of fasting mean very different things.
glucose_random.generalRangeOmittedReason: A general range for a glucose of unknown fasting state is not meaningful.

biologicalVariation.note: Unreliable for trending precisely because fasting state is unknown and dominates the variance.

altLoinc.note: IFCC-standardized, reported in mmol/mol — a SEPARATE analyte key here

mmol/mol.note: AFFINE, not proportional. NGSP% = 0.09148 x IFCC + 2.152. A pure multiplier turns the diagnostic threshold of 48 mmol/mol into 4.39%, which reads reassuringly normal — this is why the conversion model carries an offset.

hba1c.whatItMeasures: The share of your haemoglobin that has sugar stuck to it, which reflects average blood glucose over roughly the previous three months. It is not affected by what you ate this morning — but it is affected by anything that changes red-cell lifespan.

goalContext.rationale: Within the ADA-normal band, lower values sit further from the prediabetes threshold, and HbA1c is one of the measures most responsive to the fat loss and training already planned. Framed as a direction of travel rather than a cut-off — the clinically meaningful line remains 5.7%.
goalContext.source: ADA Standards of Care thresholds; the sub-band framing is interpretive.

biologicalVariation.source: Clin Biochem 2013 (PMID 23732479): CVi 1.8% overall, 1.17% by HPLC vs 2.15% by boronate affinity
biologicalVariation.methodNote: Published RCV is 5.4% by HPLC but 10.4% by boronate affinity. Where a series spans providers, use the wider figure and say so.

artifactRules.mechanism: Iron deficiency lengthens red-cell survival, giving haemoglobin more time to glycate and raising HbA1c independently of glucose.
artifactRules.discriminator: Fasting glucose, or a fructosamine, neither of which depends on red-cell lifespan.

hba1c_ifcc.loincDisplay: Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total standardized per IFCC-RMP for CDT in Blood

%.note: Exact inverse of the NGSP master equation NGSP% = 0.09148 x IFCC + 2.152, expanded to factor/offset form so the two HbA1c analytes round-trip against each other. Note the widely quoted pairing 48 mmol/mol = 6.5% is the ROUNDED value; the equation gives 6.543%.

hba1c_ifcc.whatItMeasures: The same measurement as HbA1c %, on the IFCC scale used outside the US.
hba1c_ifcc.mergeNote: Safe to display as one series after conversion, because the NGSP/IFCC master equation is exact and both codes name the same measurand.

insulin.loincNote: LOINC has no distinct 'fasting insulin' term; fasting state travels as context, not in the code.

pmol/L.reason: The uIU/mL to pmol/L factor depends on which international standard the assay is calibrated against; 6.00 and 6.945 are both in current use, a ~16% spread. Displayed in the unit the lab reported.

insulin.whatItMeasures: How much insulin your pancreas is producing to hold glucose where it is. A normal glucose achieved with a high insulin is a different situation from a normal glucose achieved with a low one.
insulin.generalRangeOmittedReason: Insulin reference intervals vary widely by assay and are not comparable across platforms.

biologicalVariation.note: RCV on the order of 65-78%. Two values are essentially uninformative.

artifactRules.mechanism: Insulin rises steeply after eating; a non-fasting insulin is not interpretable against fasting reference data.

insulin.neverComputeReason: These are clinical indices. Display them if the lab reported one; never calculate one and present it alongside measured results.

ug/L.note: Exactly equal: ng/mL = 1e-9 g / 1e-3 L = 1e-6 g/L = ug/L.

ferritin.whatItMeasures: Your stored iron — the reserve you draw on, as opposed to the iron in transit. It is also an acute-phase reactant, meaning inflammation pushes it up regardless of how much iron you actually have. That dual nature is the single most important thing to know about this test.
movedUpBy: Inflammation or infection (30-90% depending on phase)
movedDownBy: Heavy endurance training (foot-strike haemolysis, sweat and gut losses)
ferritin.generalRangeOmittedReason: Strongly sex-dependent, and an acute-phase reactant. A general range would mislead more than it informs.

goalContext.rationale: Iron-deficient non-anaemic states — ferritin low with haemoglobin still normal — measurably blunt endurance adaptation and aerobic capacity, and supplementation trials show benefit concentrated below roughly 20-30 ng/mL. Sports-medicine practice commonly uses 30-35 ng/mL as the action threshold in endurance athletes rather than the much lower figure at the bottom of a standard lab range. Directly relevant to the VO2 max goal.
goalContext.source: Sports-medicine iron-deficiency literature; ferritin <30 ng/mL as an iron-deficiency cut-point derives from the classic Guyatt diagnostic meta-analysis.
goalContext.caveat: This is a threshold for investigating, not for supplementing. Iron overload is a real harm, and ferritin alone cannot distinguish low stores from inflammation-masked low stores. Transferrin saturation and a concurrent CRP are what settle it.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 902, serum/plasma, 2 references
biologicalVariation.note: The current EFLM meta-estimate replaces the older single-study value. CVa remains an assay assumption.

artifactRules.mechanism: Ferritin is a positive acute-phase reactant. Inflammation raises it by roughly 30-90% depending on the phase, so a normal-looking ferritin during inflammation can conceal genuinely depleted stores.
artifactRules.discriminator: Transferrin saturation, and a repeat once CRP has normalised.

artifactRules.mechanism: Same mechanism — even a minor infection lifts ferritin.

iron_serum.whatItMeasures: Iron currently circulating bound to transferrin — iron in transit, not iron in store. It is one of the most variable analytes in common use, and a single value tells you very little.
movedUpBy: An iron supplement or iron-rich meal that morning
controllable: Not taking iron the morning of the test
iron_serum.generalRangeOmittedReason: Sex-dependent and so variable within a person that a general range invites over-reading.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1248, serum/plasma, 5 references
biologicalVariation.note: Very high within-person variation; a single result is unreliable. CVa remains an assay assumption.

artifactRules.mechanism: Serum iron has among the largest within-subject variation of any common analyte, plus a diurnal pattern that is not even consistent between people — one study found morning values exceeded afternoon values in only about half of subjects. It is widely regarded as an unreliable standalone marker of iron status.
artifactRules.discriminator: Read it only alongside ferritin and transferrin saturation, from a standardised morning draw.

artifactRules.mechanism: A supplement or iron-rich meal produces a large spurious rise.

tibc.loincDisplay: Iron binding capacity [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
tibc.whatItMeasures: How much iron your blood could carry if every transferrin binding site were full — effectively a measure of transferrin. It rises when iron is scarce, as the body makes more carrier.

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult range; labs vary.

biologicalVariation.note: Far more stable than serum iron — which is why saturation is more useful than iron alone.

transferrin_saturation.loincDisplay: Iron saturation [Mass Fraction] in Serum or Plasma

altLoinc.note: Iron/Iron binding capacity.total [Mass Ratio] — also appears as '% saturation'

transferrin_saturation.whatItMeasures: The fraction of your iron-carrying capacity that is actually carrying iron. Because it combines iron and TIBC, it is more informative than either alone — and unlike ferritin it is not pushed up by inflammation, which is what makes it the discriminating test when ferritin is ambiguous.

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult range. Below ~20% suggests iron-restricted erythropoiesis; sustained values above ~45-50% prompt investigation for overload.

goalContext.rationale: Saturation below roughly 20% indicates iron-restricted erythropoiesis even when haemoglobin is still normal, and it is the measure that distinguishes genuinely low iron stores from a ferritin depressed or inflated by inflammation. The discriminating test for the ferritin goalContext.
goalContext.source: Standard iron-studies interpretation; widely used cut-point.

artifactRules.mechanism: Recent iron intake inflates saturation via serum iron.

umol/L.reason: Molar conversion for a glycoprotein depends on the assumed molecular weight, which varies by glycoform and between laboratories.

transferrin.whatItMeasures: The protein that carries iron around. Measured directly rather than inferred as TIBC.

vitamin_d_25oh.loincDisplay: 25-Hydroxyvitamin D3+25-Hydroxyvitamin D2 [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
vitamin_d_25oh.loincWarning: 1989-3 is 25-OH-D3 ONLY, not D2+D3 total. Do not treat it as this analyte.
vitamin_d_25oh.whatItMeasures: Your vitamin D status — the circulating storage form, reflecting both sun exposure and intake over the past several weeks.
movedDownBy: Higher body fat (sequestration in adipose tissue)

generalRange.note: The floor is contested: the IOM considers 20 ng/mL adequate for bone health in most people, while the Endocrine Society uses 30 ng/mL as sufficiency. We show 30 as the floor and say it is contested.

goalContext.rationale: Athlete-focused guidance commonly targets 30-50 ng/mL, on observational associations with muscle function, injury and respiratory illness. Included because vitamin D is one of the few nutrients where supplementation is cheap, well-tolerated and easy to get wrong in both directions.
goalContext.source: Sports-nutrition consensus documents; the underlying evidence for performance benefit above the bone-health threshold is weak.
goalContext.caveat: Genuinely contested. Randomised trials have largely failed to show performance benefit from raising vitamin D in already-replete people. Treat this as a floor worth clearing, not a number worth chasing, and note the 100 ng/mL ceiling is a toxicity boundary, not a target.

biologicalVariation.note: Strong seasonality sits on top of the biological variation — compare like season with like season.

artifactRules.mechanism: Vitamin D swings seasonally with sun exposure; a summer-to-winter comparison mostly measures the calendar.
artifactRules.discriminator: Compare against the same season in a previous year.

artifactRules.mechanism: Some vitamin D immunoassays use streptavidin-biotin capture and are subject to high-dose biotin interference.

vitamin_b12.loincDisplay: Cobalamin (Vitamin B12) [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
vitamin_b12.whatItMeasures: Circulating B12. Note that serum B12 is a fairly blunt instrument — it can look adequate while tissue stores are depleted, which is why methylmalonic acid or homocysteine are used when the picture is unclear.
movedDownBy: Some long-term medications are associated with lower B12 — that is worth mentioning to whoever prescribes them, not acting on

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult range; the 200-350 band is often described as borderline.

vitamin_b12.linkedConcern: Folate supplementation can mask a B12 deficiency while neurological damage progresses. Any folate recommendation must check B12 first — see integration-health-records.md §9.8.

folate_serum.whatItMeasures: Circulating folate, which tracks recent intake closely — it reflects the last few days more than long-term status. RBC folate is the better measure of stores.
movedUpBy: A folate-rich meal shortly before the draw
movedDownBy: Low intake of greens and legumes
notControllable: MTHFR genotype (affects utilisation more than serum level)

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult floor; labs vary considerably.

biologicalVariation.note: Serum folate tracks recent intake, so much of the variance is diet timing rather than status.

artifactRules.mechanism: Serum folate responds within days to intake, so a single value reflects the last few meals as much as your stores.
artifactRules.discriminator: RBC folate, which reflects the previous ~3 months.

folate_serum.restrictedDietNote: Highest-priority analyte for a user's restricted dietary pattern. Leafy greens and legumes are the dominant dietary folate sources, and micronutrients.json rates folate among the highest-risk nutrients under restricted dietary pattern.

folate_rbc.loincWarning: 2286-3 is Follitropin (FSH), NOT RBC folate. This is a documented mismap trap.
folate_rbc.whatItMeasures: Folate inside red blood cells, which reflects status over the previous three months rather than the previous three meals. The better measure of actual folate stores.
movedDownBy: Sustained low intake of greens and legumes

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult floor; assay-dependent and labs vary widely.

tsh.whatItMeasures: The signal your pituitary sends to your thyroid. Counter-intuitively it moves opposite to thyroid output — a high TSH means the pituitary is shouting because it is not getting enough back.
tsh.generalRangeOmittedReason: Reference intervals differ substantially between assays and between populations, and the upper limit is actively contested. Use the lab's own.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1065, serum/plasma, 7 references

artifactRules.mechanism: High-dose biotin interferes with streptavidin-biotin immunoassays, producing falsely LOW TSH alongside falsely high free T4 and T3 — a pattern that mimics Graves' disease. The FDA has warned about the same interference falsely lowering troponin.
artifactRules.discriminator: Stop biotin 48-72h before the draw and retest.

artifactRules.mechanism: TSH has a nocturnal surge peaking around midnight to 4am and a late-afternoon trough; the swing across a day can be substantial.

free_t4.loincDisplay: Thyroxine (T4) free [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
free_t4.whatItMeasures: The unbound, biologically active fraction of thyroxine — the main hormone your thyroid produces, most of which is converted to the more active T3 in tissue.
free_t4.generalRangeOmittedReason: Highly assay-dependent; free-hormone immunoassays are not comparable between platforms.

artifactRules.mechanism: Falsely elevated by high-dose biotin in streptavidin-biotin immunoassays.

free_t3.loincDisplay: Triiodothyronine (T3) Free [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
free_t3.whatItMeasures: The active thyroid hormone at tissue level. Relevant here because it is one of the first things to fall in a sustained energy deficit — the body downregulates T4-to-T3 conversion to conserve energy, which is normal adaptive physiology rather than thyroid disease.
free_t3.generalRangeOmittedReason: Assay-dependent, and interpretation in the context of an energy deficit differs from interpretation in a clinical context.

goalContext.rationale: No numeric target — the useful signal is the DIRECTION relative to a user's own earlier values during a cut. Free T3 falling across a sustained deficit is a well-described adaptive response and one of the earlier markers that energy availability has dropped far enough to be worth managing, alongside the energy-availability checks already in guardrails.ts. Included as a directional flag rather than a range.
goalContext.source: Low-T3 syndrome and relative energy deficiency literature.
goalContext.caveat: A falling free T3 during a deliberate cut is expected physiology, not thyroid disease, and the app must never present it as the latter. If it falls alongside other energy-availability findings from guardrails.ts, that combination is the thing worth acting on — by moderating the deficit, which is nutrition-personalization's surface, not this one.

artifactRules.mechanism: Falsely elevated by high-dose biotin.

total_t3.whatItMeasures: Total T3 including the protein-bound fraction. Affected by anything that changes binding-protein levels.

testosterone_total.whatItMeasures: Total circulating testosterone, most of which is bound to SHBG and albumin and not immediately available to tissue. Relevant to this plan because sustained large energy deficits combined with high training loads lower it — which is normal, reversible physiology, and one of the costs of cutting hard.
testosterone_total.generalRangeOmittedReason: Strongly age-, sex-, assay- and time-of-day-dependent. Use the lab's own range.
testosterone_total.goalContextOmittedReason: An 'optimal testosterone' number is the single most common piece of nonsense in this product category. The useful information is direction over time from a standardised morning draw, plus the energy-availability context, not a target number.

biologicalVariation.note: The published CVi badly understates real-world variability unless draw time is controlled — diurnal variation dominates it.

artifactRules.mechanism: Testosterone peaks in the early morning and declines through the day; the fall by late afternoon is substantial in younger men and blunted in older ones. This is why guidelines specify a morning draw.
A sustained large energy deficit with high training load suppresses testosterone. This is adaptive and reversible, not a disease.

testosterone_free.loincDisplay: Testosterone Free [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

altLoinc.note: detection limit <=1.0 ng/dL — the LC-MS/dialysis reflex
[Moles/volume] by calculation. LOW CONFIDENCE: no mass/volume 'by calculation' LOINC was confirmed; US labs reporting calculated free T in pg/mL appear to reuse 2991-8. Verify against the real feed.

testosterone_free.whatItMeasures: The unbound fraction available to tissue. Worth knowing that the direct immunoassay and the equilibrium-dialysis method disagree substantially, so results from different labs are often not comparable.
testosterone_free.generalRangeOmittedReason: Method-dependent to the point that ranges are not transferable between labs.

artifactRules.mechanism: Same diurnal pattern as total testosterone.
Direct immunoassay and equilibrium dialysis give systematically different free testosterone values.

shbg.loincDisplay: Sex hormone binding globulin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma

ug/dL.reason: SHBG is a glycoprotein of roughly 90 kDa with variable glycosylation; there is no dependable fixed molar conversion.

shbg.whatItMeasures: The protein that binds most of your circulating testosterone. It determines how much of a given total testosterone is actually available, which is why total testosterone alone can mislead.
shbg.neverComputeReason: Both are clinical calculations. Display if the lab reported one.

estradiol.whatItMeasures: The main oestrogen. In men it comes largely from aromatisation of testosterone in adipose tissue, so it tends to track body fat and testosterone together.
estradiol.generalRangeOmittedReason: Sex-dependent, and in cycling women the menstrual cycle dominates the variance entirely.

biologicalVariation.note: Figure is for men. In cycling women, cycle phase swamps biological variation entirely and RCV is not applicable without cycle-day metadata.

artifactRules.mechanism: Immunoassays are unreliable at the low concentrations typical in men; LC-MS/MS is the accurate method.

dhea_s.loincDisplay: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA-S) [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
dhea_s.whatItMeasures: An adrenal androgen precursor. More stable through the day than cortisol, which is why it is sometimes used as a rough adrenal-output marker.
dhea_s.generalRangeOmittedReason: Falls steeply and continuously with age; a single adult range is misleading.

hs_crp.loincDisplay: C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma by High sensitivity method

nmol/L.reason: CRP is a ~120 kDa pentamer; molar conversion depends on an assumed molecular weight that is not consistently applied.

hs_crp.whatItMeasures: Low-grade systemic inflammation, measured sensitively enough to resolve the small differences that matter for cardiovascular risk. It is exquisitely sensitive to anything acute — an infection, or a hard training session — which is both its strength and the reason a single value is nearly useless.
movedUpBy: Hard or unaccustomed training in the previous days
movedDownBy: Being genuinely rested at the draw
controllable: Being rested and well at the draw
hs_crp.generalRangeOmittedReason: Better expressed as the AHA/CDC risk strata than as a single range — see goalContext.

goalContext.rationale: The AHA/CDC cardiovascular risk strata are <1 mg/L low, 1-3 average, >3 high, with anything above 10 mg/L treated as acute inflammation to be investigated and retested rather than interpreted as risk. Well-established and directly actionable.
goalContext.source: AHA/CDC scientific statement on markers of inflammation in cardiovascular disease.

strata.label: above 10 mg/L — treated as acute inflammation, not as a risk category. Retest when well and rested.

goalContext.caveat: The risk stratification assumes two measurements at least two weeks apart, taken when free of acute illness, with anything above 10 mg/L discarded and repeated. A single hs-CRP is not a risk assessment.

biologicalVariation.source: PLOS One 2024 meta-analysis: CVi median 44%, range 27-76%, ICC 0.62
biologicalVariation.note: RCV exceeds 100%. A value must more than double to be distinguishable from noise. Requires >=4 results before any direction is drawn.

artifactRules.mechanism: hs-CRP rises for days after hard or unaccustomed training, particularly eccentric work.
artifactRules.discriminator: Retest after a week of easy training.

artifactRules.mechanism: Values above 10 mg/L reflect acute inflammation rather than baseline cardiovascular risk. The standard protocol discards them.
artifactRules.discriminator: Retest when well and rested; two draws at least two weeks apart.

artifactRules.mechanism: Any infection raises hs-CRP substantially.

hs_crp.pairsWithNote: A concurrent hs-CRP is what tells you whether a ferritin is reporting iron stores or inflammation.

crp.loincDisplay: C reactive protein [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
crp.whatItMeasures: The same protein as hs-CRP, measured by a less sensitive assay aimed at detecting frank inflammation rather than resolving the low end.
controllable: Being well and rested at the draw

generalRange.note: Standard-sensitivity CRP is usually reported against a ceiling around 10 mg/L; below that it cannot resolve differences.

crp.goalContextOmittedReason: The cardiovascular strata require a high-sensitivity assay. Applying them to a standard CRP is invalid.

artifactRules.mechanism: Rises after hard training.

crp.doNotMergeReason: Different assays with different sensitivity floors. Merging them corrupts the cardiovascular strata.

creatinine.whatItMeasures: A breakdown product of creatine from muscle, cleared by the kidneys. It is used as a kidney marker on the assumption that production is steady — an assumption that does not hold in someone with a lot of muscle who supplements creatine.
movedUpBy: Intense exercise in the previous days
notControllable: Muscle mass, in the short term
creatinine.generalRangeOmittedReason: Strongly dependent on muscle mass and sex. A general range mislabels muscular people.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1501, serum/plasma, 17 references

critical.note: Typical hospital limits run 5-10 mg/dL or a large delta from baseline; ours is set lower because a consumer with no baseline context should be pushed to a clinician sooner. NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW.

artifactRules.mechanism: Supplemental creatine can modestly raise serum creatinine through turnover of the larger creatine pool without a corresponding reduction in measured filtration in healthy trial participants. That does not prove an abnormal result is harmless.
artifactRules.discriminator: Ask a clinician whether combined creatinine-cystatin C eGFR or measured GFR is appropriate when creatinine is unreliable.
artifactRules.magnitudeNote: Direction is supported by randomized trials; individual magnitude is not predictable, so the app never numerically corrects it.

artifactRules.mechanism: Intense exercise raises creatinine transiently through muscle turnover and haemoconcentration.
artifactRules.discriminator: Redraw after 72h of easy training and good hydration.

artifactRules.mechanism: Creatinine scales with muscle mass, so a muscular person sits higher on a range built from the general population.

cystatin_c.loincDisplay: Cystatin C [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma
cystatin_c.loincNote: NOT verified against loinc.org during research — the web budget was exhausted. Confirm before relying on it.

nmol/L.reason: Cystatin C is a ~13 kDa protein; molar conversion depends on an assumed molecular weight that is not applied consistently.

cystatin_c.whatItMeasures: A small protein used to estimate kidney filtration. It is less dependent on muscle mass than creatinine, but thyroid status, corticosteroids, inflammation and body composition can also affect it. Combined creatinine-cystatin C eGFR is generally more accurate than either marker alone.
cystatin_c.generalRangeOmittedReason: Assay-dependent; use the lab's own range.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1513, serum/plasma, 5 references

egfr.loincDisplay: Glomerular filtration rate [Volume Rate/Area] in Serum, Plasma or Blood by Creatinine-based formula (CKD-EPI 2021)/1.73 sq M

altLoinc.note: CKD-EPI generic — still very common in live feeds
Creatinine + cystatin C, CKD-EPI 2021 — the preferred equation for creatine users
CKD-EPI among non-black population — legacy, being retired post-2021

egfr.whatItMeasures: An estimate of kidney filtration rate calculated from creatinine — not a measurement. Because it inverts creatinine, everything that raises creatinine lowers eGFR whether or not the kidneys are involved.
egfr.generalRangeOmittedReason: Equation-dependent, and legacy race-adjusted equations are not comparable with CKD-EPI 2021.
egfr.goalContextOmittedReason: There is no athlete-optimal eGFR. Higher is not better.

biologicalVariation.derivationNote: Biological variation is published for creatinine, not eGFR. CKD-EPI is roughly a power function of creatinine with exponent about -1.2, so eGFR's CV is approximately 1.2x creatinine's and its RCV is asymmetric before any log-normal consideration. See Front Med 2022 eGFR BV meta-analysis, which was not reachable during research.

egfr.criticalOmittedReason: A low eGFR in a creatine-supplementing, muscular person is the single most likely false alarm this catalogue could generate. Kidney concern routes through creatinine's threshold, not this one.

artifactRules.mechanism: Creatine supplementation can raise creatinine and therefore lower creatinine-based eGFR without reducing measured filtration in healthy trial participants. It is one possible explanation, not a diagnosis and never a reason to suppress an abnormal result.
artifactRules.discriminator: Clinical context plus combined creatinine-cystatin C eGFR (LOINC 98980-6), or measured GFR when needed.

artifactRules.mechanism: MDRD, CKD-EPI and CKD-EPI 2021 give systematically different numbers, and the 2021 revision removed the race coefficient.
artifactRules.discriminator: Compare only within one equation; the LOINC code identifies which was used.

artifactRules.mechanism: Exercise-induced creatinine rise lowers calculated eGFR transiently.

bun.loincDisplay: Urea nitrogen [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

mmol/L.note: The SI value is MOLAR UREA, not molar nitrogen. BUN mg/dL x 0.357 = urea mmol/L; this factor is the inverse. Carries a visible note in the UI.

bun.whatItMeasures: Nitrogen from urea, the end product of protein breakdown, cleared by the kidneys. It rises with high protein intake and with dehydration as readily as with reduced kidney function — which limits what it says on its own.

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult range. High-protein diets sit at the top of it routinely.

artifactRules.mechanism: BUN scales with protein intake. A cutting diet at 2+ g/kg protein routinely sits at or above the top of a general reference range without anything being wrong.
artifactRules.discriminator: Creatinine and eGFR, which do not track protein intake the same way.

artifactRules.mechanism: Dehydration concentrates urea and raises BUN disproportionately to creatinine.

alt.loincDisplay: Alanine aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma
alt.whatItMeasures: An enzyme concentrated in the liver, released when liver cells are stressed. It is also present in skeletal muscle, which is why hard training raises it.
alt.generalRangeOmittedReason: Reference ceilings vary substantially between labs and there is ongoing debate about lowering them.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1495, serum/plasma, 6 references

artifactRules.mechanism: ALT is present in skeletal muscle as well as liver, so muscle damage from training raises it. This is routinely misread as liver injury in people who lift.
artifactRules.discriminator: GGT — it is liver-specific and unaffected by muscle. A raised ALT with a normal GGT points away from the liver.

ast.loincDisplay: Aspartate aminotransferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma
ast.whatItMeasures: An enzyme found in liver, heart and skeletal muscle. Because it is more abundant in muscle than ALT, training raises it more — an AST above ALT in someone lifting hard is usually muscle, not liver.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1496, serum/plasma, 5 references

artifactRules.mechanism: AST is abundant in skeletal muscle — more so than ALT — so training raises it preferentially.
artifactRules.discriminator: GGT, which muscle does not raise; and CK, which confirms the muscle source.

alp.loincDisplay: Alkaline phosphatase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma
alp.whatItMeasures: An enzyme from liver, bile ducts and bone. Because bone is a major source, growth and bone turnover raise it independently of the liver.
alp.generalRangeOmittedReason: Strongly age-dependent — adolescents run far higher than adults — so a single adult range misleads.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1690, serum/plasma, 13 references

ggt.loincDisplay: Gamma glutamyl transferase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma
ggt.whatItMeasures: A liver and bile-duct enzyme that skeletal muscle does not contain — which is exactly why it is the useful companion test when a raised ALT or AST might just be training.

albumin.whatItMeasures: The main protein in blood. It reflects liver synthesis and nutritional state over weeks, but it also moves with hydration — dehydration concentrates it.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1515, serum/plasma, 16 references
biologicalVariation.clinicalFloorNote: The clinical floor is a product heuristic and still needs clinician review.

artifactRules.mechanism: Moving from lying to standing causes roughly 5-10% haemoconcentration within about 30 minutes, and dehydration does the same. That shift exceeds this analyte's entire reference change value.
artifactRules.discriminator: Standardise draw conditions; interpret alongside haematocrit, which moves the same way.

bilirubin_total.whatItMeasures: A breakdown product of haemoglobin, processed by the liver. A mildly raised value in an otherwise well person is very often Gilbert's syndrome, a common and benign inherited variation — and fasting raises it further.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 540, serum/plasma, 8 references

artifactRules.mechanism: Fasting raises unconjugated bilirubin, markedly so in people with the Gilbert's variant.
artifactRules.discriminator: Redraw non-fasting; a fractionated bilirubin showing a predominantly unconjugated rise with normal liver enzymes is the classic pattern.

mEq/L.note: Monovalent — mEq/L and mmol/L are numerically identical.

sodium.whatItMeasures: Sodium concentration, which the body defends within very tight limits. It is more a measure of water balance than of salt intake.
movedDownBy: Excess water intake, particularly during long endurance sessions
controllable: Hydration strategy, especially around long training

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1500, serum/plasma, 12 references
biologicalVariation.clinicalFloorNote: The 5 mmol/L clinical floor is a product heuristic and still needs clinician review.

critical.note: Set outside the CAP envelope. Typical hospital limits are <120 and >160, with institutional lows spanning 110-130 and highs 147-170. NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW.

potassium.whatItMeasures: Potassium concentration, tightly regulated because heart rhythm depends on it. Most body potassium is inside cells, so the serum number is a small window onto a large pool.
movedUpBy: Haemolysis of the sample (very common cause of a spurious high)
controllable: Not clenching the fist during the draw

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1499, serum/plasma, 11 references

critical.note: Typical hospital limits are <2.5 and >6.5 (CAP Q-Probes). Set marginally outside. NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW.

artifactRules.mechanism: Haemolysis releases potassium from red cells into the serum and can raise the measured value by 0.5 mmol/L or more, fabricating hyperkalaemia. Labs usually flag it.
artifactRules.note: This rule NEVER suppresses a critical-value prompt — it is shown alongside it.

chloride.whatItMeasures: Chloride concentration, which generally tracks sodium and contributes to the acid-base picture.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1512, serum/plasma, 11 references

co2_total.loincDisplay: Carbon dioxide, total [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma
co2_total.loincNote: Total CO2 on a metabolic panel — NOT 11557-6, which is blood-gas pCO2.
co2_total.whatItMeasures: Mostly bicarbonate — the body's main acid buffer. Relevant to endurance work, since buffering capacity is part of what sets tolerance for high-intensity efforts.

calcium_total.loincNote: Ionised calcium is a separate analyte (38230-9) and is not interchangeable with total.
calcium_total.whatItMeasures: Total calcium, about half of which is bound to albumin. Because of that binding, a low albumin lowers total calcium without changing the physiologically active ionised fraction.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1087, serum/plasma, 20 references
biologicalVariation.clinicalFloorNote: The clinical floor is a product heuristic and still needs clinician review.

critical.note: Typical hospital limits are <6.0 and >13.0 (CAP Q-Probes). NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW.

artifactRules.mechanism: About half of total calcium is albumin-bound, so an abnormal albumin shifts total calcium without changing the active ionised fraction.
artifactRules.discriminator: An ionised calcium, which is unaffected by albumin.

artifactRules.mechanism: Haemoconcentration from posture or dehydration raises protein-bound analytes including calcium.

magnesium.whatItMeasures: Magnesium in the blood — which is roughly 1% of your body's magnesium. The rest is in bone and inside cells, and serum is defended at the expense of those stores. A normal serum magnesium therefore does NOT rule out depletion, which is unusual among the tests on a metabolic panel and worth knowing.
magnesium.goalContextOmittedReason: Serum magnesium is too weak a proxy for status to justify a goal range. The food log is the better evidence here.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1110, serum/plasma, 11 references

artifactRules.mechanism: Only about 1% of body magnesium is extracellular, and serum concentration is maintained by drawing on bone and intracellular stores. A normal serum magnesium is consistent with meaningful depletion.
artifactRules.discriminator: There is no good routine test. Dietary intake over time is the more informative evidence.

phosphate.whatItMeasures: Phosphate, which partners with calcium in bone and is central to ATP. It has a diurnal rhythm and falls after carbohydrate intake.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 242, serum/plasma, 17 references

mmol/L.note: Per-heme-monomer convention used in the Netherlands and Scandinavia. Carries a visible note in the UI because the convention is not universal.

hemoglobin.whatItMeasures: The oxygen-carrying protein in your red cells. Directly relevant to VO2 max, because oxygen delivery is one of its limiting factors — but also easily distorted by hydration and by training-induced plasma volume expansion.
movedDownBy: Endurance training (plasma volume expansion dilutes it)
hemoglobin.generalRangeOmittedReason: Strongly sex-dependent, and endurance-trained people legitimately run lower than the general population.
hemoglobin.goalContextOmittedReason: Higher is not straightforwardly better; the useful signal is direction alongside ferritin and saturation.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1522, whole blood, 16 references
biologicalVariation.clinicalFloorNote: The clinical floor is a product heuristic and still needs clinician review.

critical.note: Typical hospital low-critical limits run 5.0-7.0 g/dL, highs around 20. NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW.

artifactRules.mechanism: Endurance training expands plasma volume, diluting haemoglobin while total red-cell mass is normal or increased. This is sometimes called athlete's pseudoanaemia, and it is an adaptation rather than a deficiency.
artifactRules.discriminator: Ferritin and transferrin saturation — normal iron studies with a low-normal haemoglobin in a trained endurance athlete points to dilution.

artifactRules.mechanism: Posture and hydration shift plasma volume 5-10% within half an hour, which exceeds this analyte's reference change value.

hematocrit.loincDisplay: Hematocrit [Volume Fraction] of Blood by Automated count
hematocrit.whatItMeasures: The proportion of your blood volume that is red cells. Moves with haemoglobin and with the same hydration caveats.
hematocrit.generalRangeOmittedReason: Sex-dependent; endurance athletes legitimately run lower.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1524, whole blood, 8 references

hematocrit.criticalOmittedReason: Haemoglobin carries the threshold; duplicating it here would double-fire on the same physiology.

artifactRules.mechanism: Plasma volume shifts of 5-10% from posture or hydration move haematocrit directly.
Plasma volume expansion from endurance training lowers haematocrit without reducing red-cell mass.

rbc.loincDisplay: Erythrocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count
rbc.whatItMeasures: How many red cells per unit volume. Same hydration caveats as haemoglobin and haematocrit.

artifactRules.mechanism: Plasma volume shifts move all three red-cell measures together.

wbc.loincDisplay: Leukocytes [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count
wbc.whatItMeasures: Circulating white cells. It rises with infection but also transiently with hard exercise and with stress, which is why a modest elevation in an otherwise well person often means nothing.
movedUpBy: Hard exercise in the hours before the draw

critical.note: Typical hospital limits run 0.5-2.0 low and 30-100 high. NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW.

artifactRules.mechanism: Exercise causes a transient leukocytosis via demargination and catecholamine release.

platelets.loincDisplay: Platelets [#/volume] in Blood by Automated count
platelets.whatItMeasures: The cells that form clots. Rises with inflammation and with iron deficiency; falls in a number of conditions.

critical.note: Typical hospital limits run 20-50 low and 1000-1500 high. NEEDS CLINICIAN REVIEW.

mcv.loincDisplay: MCV [Entitic mean volume] in Red Blood Cells by Automated count
mcv.whatItMeasures: The average size of your red cells. Small cells point toward iron limitation, large ones toward B12 or folate — which makes it a useful companion to the nutrient tests.

biologicalVariation.clinicalFloorNote: The most stable index on the panel — RCV about 4%. Without the floor, trivial moves flag.

fmol.reason: The pg to fmol conversion uses the haemoglobin-monomer molecular weight convention, which is not applied consistently between laboratories.

mch.whatItMeasures: Average haemoglobin per red cell. Tracks MCV closely.

mchc.loincDisplay: MCHC [Entitic Mass/volume] in Red Blood Cells by Automated count
mchc.whatItMeasures: Haemoglobin concentration within the red cells themselves.

rdw.loincDisplay: Erythrocyte [DistWidth] in Blood by Automated count
rdw.whatItMeasures: How variable your red cells are in size. It often rises before MCV moves, which makes it an early hint of an emerging iron, B12 or folate problem.

neutrophils_pct.loincDisplay: Neutrophils/Leukocytes in Blood by Automated count
neutrophils_pct.whatItMeasures: The share of white cells that are neutrophils, the first responders to bacterial infection. Exercise transiently raises them.

artifactRules.mechanism: Exercise causes transient neutrophilia.

lymphocytes_pct.loincDisplay: Lymphocytes/Leukocytes in Blood by Automated count
lymphocytes_pct.whatItMeasures: The share of white cells that are lymphocytes. Falls transiently after hard exercise, which has been studied extensively in athletes.

artifactRules.mechanism: Post-exercise lymphopenia is well described and transient.

creatine_kinase.loincDisplay: Creatine kinase [Enzymatic activity/volume] in Serum or Plasma
creatine_kinase.whatItMeasures: An enzyme released when muscle is damaged. In someone training seriously it is much more a training-load marker than a disease marker — which is why it needs careful framing rather than alarm.
movedDownBy: Adaptation to a training stimulus (the repeated-bout effect)
creatine_kinase.generalRangeOmittedReason: General-population ceilings are routinely and harmlessly exceeded by people who lift. Applying one here would generate constant false alarms.

biologicalVariation.source: EFLM BV API meta calculation, analyte 1502, serum/plasma, 3 references

creatine_kinase.criticalOmittedReason: Deliberately excluded from critical prompts despite appearing on some hospital lists. Unaccustomed eccentric training routinely produces CK multiples that would trip any threshold worth having, so a prompt here would be wrong far more often than right.

artifactRules.mechanism: Unaccustomed resistance or eccentric work raises CK enormously — multiples of the upper reference limit are routine — peaking 24-72 hours afterwards and taking up to a week to normalise. It is frequently mistaken for rhabdomyolysis or statin myopathy.
artifactRules.discriminator: Retest after 7 days without hard training. A CK that normalises fully was training.

uric_acid.loincNote: The LOINC component is 'Urate', not 'Uric acid'.
uric_acid.whatItMeasures: The end product of purine metabolism. It rises with dehydration, with alcohol, with high purine intake, and — relevant here — during rapid fat loss.

generalRange.note: Commonly used adult ceiling for men; women's is lower.

artifactRules.mechanism: Ketone bodies compete with urate for renal excretion, so uric acid rises during rapid fat loss and ketosis. Directly relevant to an aggressive cut.
